The single large nucleus remains suspended in the center of the vacuole by a number of cytoplasmic strands. The cytoplasm of Spirogyra consists of spirally arranged ribbon shape chloroplast. The number of chloroplast varies in number from one to sixteen in different species. In each chloroplast, nodules like protein bodies are present. These protein bodies store starch, and is known as pyrenoids.

Fig: 2.4.5 Cell structure of Spirogyra Reproduction Spirogyra reproduces by vegetative, asexual and sexual method. 1. Vegetative method: Vegetative reproduction takes place by fragmentation under favourable condition. It is the common method of reproduction. The dissociation of filament takes place by mechanical injury, death of intercalary cells, etc. Each fragment later independently forms long filament of Spirogyra.
Fig: 2.4.6 Fragmentation in Spirogyra Biology, Grade 11 | 113

Asexual reproduction is less common in Spirogyra. It takes place by the formation of aplanosproes, akinetes and azygospores. Under unfavourable condition, the protoplast of each vegetative cell shrinks and develops a wall around it to form aplanospores. Each aplanospore germinates to form a new filament. Akinetes are thick walled cells of filament formed by formation of additional wall under unfavourable condition. On return of favourable conditions , each akinete germinates into a new filament. Sometimes the gametes are failed to fuse in some species. These gametes round off and secrete a thick walled which surrounds them to form azygospores or parthenospores. Each parthenospore gives new filament during favourable condition.

3. Sexual reproduction The Spirogyra shows conjugation type of sexual reproduction. Conjugation is an isogamous type. It involves the fusion of entire contents of the two morphologically similar unspecialized vegetative cells, known as gametangia. Sexual reproduction takes place towards the end of the growing season. It is of two types: a. Scalariform conjugation (Ladder type): It is the most common method and takes place at night between two different filaments (i.e. in heterothallic species of Spirogyra). In this process, two filaments of different strains come close and lie side by side. Both filaments get surrounded by common sheath of mucilage. Now, special conjugating cells of these two filaments develop small outgrowths known as protuberances or papillae in opposite direction. The papillae elongate and come in contact with each other. At the point of contact, the tips of these outgrowths dissolve by an enzyme, cytase and form hollow tubular structure called conjugation tube. At this stage it resembles as ladder. Hence, the conjugation is called scalariform (Gr. Scala=ladder; forma=shape). After the formation of conjugation tube, the protoplasm of one cell functions as male gametangium and other cell as female gametangium. The protoplasts of gametangium shrink to form gametes. The protoplasmic content of male gametangia moves towards the female gametangia though conjugation tube and fuse to form zygote. The zygote secrete wall around it, which is called zygospore. The cells of another filament remain empty.
Fig: 2.4.8 Different stages of Scalariform conjugation in Spirogyra

b. Lateral conjugation It is of rare type and involves the fusion of gametes from two adjacent cells of the same filament in monocious or homothallic species. It is of two types: i. Indirect lateral conjugation: Indirect lateral conjugation is the common method of lateral conjugation. In this conjugation, two adjacent cells of same filament function as male and female gametangium. The lateral outgrowth of the two adjacent cells forms papillae. The papillae grow in size and come in contact with each other. The common wall between them dissolves by enzyme and hollow tubular outgrowth is formed known as lateral tube. The protoplasmic content of one cell which functions as male gametangium behaves as male gamete and moves through the lateral tube to female gametangium which behaves as female gamete. The protoplasmic content of both male and female gametangia is fused to form diploid zygospore.

Fig: 2.4.9 Different stages of indirect lateral conjugation in Spirogyra ii. Direct lateral conjugation It is primitive type of conjugation occurring in few species. In this conjugation, the lower cell of the two adjacent cells gets enlarged and forms barrel shaped female gamete, while upper one behaves as male gamete. The male gamete develops pointed boring organ which creates pore mechanically or enzymatically on middle of the septum. The protoplasm of male gamete migrates through the pore and fuses with female gamete to form zygospore.
